---
title: "R reference: the small vocabulary we use"
---

These examples assume that you opened the extracted course `.Rproj` file.
Use **RStudio's R console** for R, not a terminal waiting for shell commands.
Save reusable code in an R script or your `.Rmd` report.

## Objects and functions

```r
lengths_mm <- c(12, 15, 18)
mean(lengths_mm)
sd(lengths_mm)
length(lengths_mm)
```

`<-` assigns a value to a name. `c()` combines values into a vector.
`mean()` computes an arithmetic mean, `sd()` a sample standard deviation, and
`length()` the number of elements. Text needs quotes, as in `"control"`.
R is case-sensitive: `Length` and `length` are different names.

## Import, inspect, and calculate

```r
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

seedlings <- read_csv("data/seedlings.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
head(seedlings)
names(seedlings)
nrow(seedlings)
glimpse(seedlings)

seedlings <- seedlings |>
  mutate(growth_mm = final_mm - initial_mm)
```

`|>` means “take this result and pass it to the next function”. `mutate()` adds
or changes columns. A calculation creates a derived measurement; it does not
change the original CSV unless you explicitly write a file.

```r
treated <- seedlings |>
  filter(treatment == "treated")

summary_table <- seedlings |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_mm = mean(growth_mm), sd_mm = sd(growth_mm),
            .groups = "drop")
```

`==` compares values; it does not assign. `filter()` selects rows.
`group_by()` tells `summarise()` which groups to summarise. For missing data,
report both available and missing counts rather than silently dropping records.

## A plot and an exported file

```r
growth_plot <- ggplot(seedlings, aes(x = treatment, y = growth_mm)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 7)) +
  labs(x = "Allocation", y = "Seven-day growth (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()
growth_plot
ggsave("output/growth.png", plot = growth_plot, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 150)
write_csv(summary_table, "output/growth-summary.csv")
```

The `+` joins layers in a ggplot. Horizontal jitter separates overlapping
points; `height = 0` preserves their measured values. `ggsave()` needs an output
folder that already exists; the course project includes one.

## Missing is not zero

```r
x <- c(10, NA, 20)
is.na(x)
sum(is.na(x))
sum(!is.na(x))
mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
```

`NA` denotes an unavailable value. `na.rm = TRUE` computes from available
observations; it does not justify missingness or replace a report of how many
were missing. The mean here is 15 from two available values.

## Error recovery

| Message or symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| “object not found” | Spelling, case, and whether the line creating it ran |
| “could not find function” | Whether the right package was loaded |
| “cannot open file” | Project, path, filename case, and local versus remote computer |
| Console prompt is `+` | Unfinished quotes/brackets; press Esc and fix the expression |
| Report fails but console works | An object or package may exist only in your interactive session |

Use `?mean`, `?t.test`, or `?lm` to open R's help for a named function. Ask for
help with the exact error and the smallest relevant code, without credentials.
